The Supreme Court has told every court in India to stop recording the caste or religion of litigants in case papers. Yet the habit lingers in many filings. Shama Sharma v. Kishan Kumar THE FACTS A family transfer petition listed the parties' caste Counsel said the registry would object if the memo of parties differed from the lower courts', so caste was carried forward. THE DIRECTION No caste or religion in the memo of parties In the Supreme Court, and in every High Court and subordinate court, even if it appeared in the courts below. Justices Hima Kohli and Ahsanuddin Amanullah. "Such a practice is to be shunned and must be ceased forthwith." Supreme Court of India, Shama Sharma v. Kishan Kumar Adv. Ashwani Kumar 02 / 07

A CONSISTENT DIRECTION Courts are closing the door on caste labels October 2023 A Supreme Court bench led by Justice Abhay S. Oka disapproves of courts citing a party's caste or religion in judgment cause-titles. January–February 2024 Shama Sharma order; the Supreme Court issues a circular, and High Courts (Gujarat, Gauhati, Karnataka and others) follow with their own. September 2025 The Allahabad High Court bars caste of accused and witnesses in FIRs and police records; Uttar Pradesh implements it, except for SC/ST Act cases. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 03 / 07

Why caste labels damage justice 1 It erodes the image of neutrality. A court that labels litigants by caste signals that identity is relevant, even when it isn't. 2 It invites bias. Identity is on the page before the facts are. Conscious or not, prejudice can follow. 3 It can be used against marginalised litigants. A caste label can become a tool to prejudice their case, turning a legal dispute into a social one. 4 It disrupts the process. Arguments drift from merits to identity, and courts become stages for social conflict. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 04 / 07

THE BALANCE When caste is a legal fact, not a label CAN BE PLEADED CAN BE PLEADED SC/ST (Prevention of Reservation and service Atrocities) Act matters Caste is an ingredient of the Where the dispute is about a offence, so it must appear where category, quota or caste relevant. certificate. The rule targets the memo of parties and cause-titles: how a litigant is identified. Where caste is the issue in dispute, it belongs in the pleadings as a fact, argued on evidence. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 07

Clean case papers Drop caste and religion from the memo of parties Even if the lower court's papers had them. Identify parties properly Name, parentage, age, occupation and address are enough. Plead caste only when it's an ingredient Atrocities Act, reservation or certificate disputes. Cite the order if the registry objects Shama Sharma (SC, 10.01.2024) and your High Court's circular. Brief your clients Explain why their identity won't appear, and why that helps them. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 07

TA K E AWAY A litigant is a party, not a caste. Equality before law (Article 14) starts with how we write the first page of a case. Every advocate who drops a caste label from a memo of parties makes the system look, and act, a little more like the justice it promises. Adv.
